featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Galande
featured_reviews.review_text: Looking for lots of tempting vegetarian food options with pocket friendly prices, this is the place. and whoever says that theres hardly few dishes to choose for veg dining then you must visit this restaurant. Perfect place for family and friends to enjoy. Food is served with eye catchy garnishing and not too oily. Taste is just awesome. You can choose any cuisine you wont be disappointed. Pot rice is widely choosen dish here which is adequately enough for 2 people.

featured_reviews.name: Sarvesh Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve had the pesto pasta from Annamaya twice, and both times it was absolutely wonderful—yummy and just the way I expected it to be. On both occasions, I opted for takeaway, and the quality truly stood out. It’s definitely worth the price.

However, the second time I ordered through Swiggy, and it took about 50 minutes for the delivery. The taste wasn’t quite the same after the delay, which affected the overall experience.

I’d definitely recommend having it fresh for the best flavor and experience.

featured_reviews.name: Swad Stories
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is one of the best resturants in Lalbaug Mumbai. They have a wide range of variety in cuisines that includes north Indian,  Chinese, Italian, Mexican.......
There are a lot of options in soup but I personally like their seven treasure soup. Also there are a lot of options in starters. Their paneer chilly and loaded nachos is a good option. In mains also there is a lot of options including sizzlers, pizza, pasta, rice and many more. Try their seven treasure rice with gravy. Overall a good place for food lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant Sail
featured_reviews.review_text:
Starting with the ambience the place was happening with great Greek art work on the wall which speaks alot. They have a separate seating area for groups.
We ordered -
Orange Sunrise Mocktail 🍹
Pink Lady Smoothie 😋
Mushrooms Cappuccino Soup 🍄🥣
Greek Salad 🥗
Picante Pizza 🍕
Paneer Tikka Biryani 😍

Talking about the food they have Greek Cuisine, we started with Mushrooms Cappuccino soup which I would rank as the best veg soup i ever had. Then we had Greek salad which was good to have with a good taste it was full of vegies and the taste of masala which makes it more delicious. Later we had Picante pizza 🍕 which was cheese loaded with paneer and delicious in taste. The showstopper was the Paneer Tikka Biryani Laccha Style which was super delicious and loaded with spices and paneer which made it more delicious to have.
The drinks were very refreshing specially the orange sunrise mocktail and the pink Lady Smoothie was so good.

Overall was a great experience with great ambience and the service which they provided was amazing

Food - 5/5
Ambience - 5/5
Service - 5/5

In terms of the experience, the ambience and hospitality is top notch. The staff is cordial and  well dressed, as if, a personal butler for each table in the form of a waiter.

The lip-smacking food is served fresh from the chef’s table top along with condiments, spices, popadums (read papad) that add to the amazing flavour of the food served.

I ordered multiple delicacies some of which were bang-on recommendations, courtesy of the waiter.

They also offer a complimentary cake for special occasions if you inform the staff well in advance

All-in-all, apart from the traditional Indian decor of elephants claiming royalty, the place seems to meet the expectation of a royal food serving place.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Akash Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Jyran at the Sofitel BKC last Friday (Jan 16) with a group of friends, and it was the perfect start to the weekend. The "Modern Nawabi" ambiance and the stunning metal elephant sculpture in the courtyard set the stage for a truly upscale dining experience.
We started with the Aloo Chaat, which was a delightful explosion of tangy and spicy flavors. For starters, the Veg Aloo was beautifully prepared, but the Chicken Tandoori was the clear standout, perfectly charred, smoky, and incredibly succulent. It is rare to find tandoori chicken that remains this moist while packing such a deep punch of traditional spices.
For the main course, the Veg Dum Biryani was a masterclass in slow-cooked perfection. The aroma upon opening the "dum" seal was divine, with every grain of long-grain basmati rice infused with saffron and aromatic spices.
The service was impeccable despite the Friday night rush, making us feel truly welcomed. If you’re looking for authentic Northwest Frontier cuisine in a luxury setting, Jyran is the place to be. I can’t wait to return with the squad!

We started with the Veg Seekh Kebab and Rajma Galouti Kebab, and both were exceptional—flavourful, well-balanced, and beautifully prepared. For the main course, the Achari Paneer was packed with authentic flavours, while the Dal Makhni was simply outstanding and among the best we’ve had in a long time.

The highlight of the evening was undoubtedly the Jyran Special Falooda. Its unique presentation and distinctive taste made for a memorable finish to an already fantastic meal.

A special mention to Chef Kishan Samant for curating such delicious dishes and ensuring a remarkable culinary experience. His passion and attention to detail were evident in every course.

Kartik and Rahul were very courteous and served us with a smile.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy great food, elegant ambience, and live music in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Jyran – Tandoor Dining, and I must say the experience was truly exceptional. From the very moment I arrived, the warmth of the welcome and the graceful way I was escorted to my table set the tone for a wonderful evening.

I would especially like to appreciate Santosh, who is an incredibly helpful and attentive staff member. His service was outstanding throughout the evening. He handled everything with great professionalism — from suggesting beverages that perfectly complemented the meal to ensuring that every detail at the table was taken care of seamlessly. His command of English and his polite, confident communication style added a very refined touch to the overall experience.

When I arrived, I was honestly not in the best mood. However, Santosh’s courteous behavior, pleasant personality, and engaging yet respectful conversation completely transformed my evening. It is rare to come across someone who not only serves food but also uplifts the guest’s mood with such natural hospitality.

The food was absolutely delicious, rich in authentic flavors, and beautifully presented. Combined with such impeccable service, the entire dining experience felt truly luxurious and memorable.

I would highly recommend Jyran to my friends and relatives — not only for its exquisite cuisine but also for the exceptional service that makes every guest feel valued and special.

featured_reviews.review_text:
TOTALLY AVOID WASTING RS 5000.

At the onset this is probably one of the most expensive Buffets you would be having in Mumbai, priced at over 4300 plus taxes for a Dinner on a Weekday for an adult. Add to that, even as a gold accor member you probably get 20-30 percent instead of the normal 50 percent for 2 people is taxing.

The spread is decent, the variety in principal is there, but in terms of the taste and the quality of food, it’s really one of the poorest of the five stars , even considering the Leela and Lalit brands in Mumbai whose lay is very modest compared to this.

At almost 5000 you expect
1. Your veg sushi not being dumped in the refrigerator for you to pick up, questioning when it was made !

2. No juice , cold drink or mocktails are part of this offering. An advise to the team, you’re charging 5000 offering a drink probably at times could feel better than half the items on the menu.

3. I have seen just one Langarwaali daal the last 4 times I have gone here, to be honest , a Dal Makhani is the norm, if not that a top of the line dal Tadka.

4. Some dishes are borderline tasteless and on the menu just to increase the offerings on paper / website
A. Sushi - cold, refrigerated, and tasted as if it was made with zero interest.
B. Pizza Margerita- looked like an Udipi version not one served at a top 5 star, see the pictures yourself.
C. Fattoush salad, I mean if anyone has had a look at what they serve with that name, it’s embarrassing.
D. Starters like paneer tikka seem like lying there unattended for hours.
E. Many of the deserts too seem just good looking and tasting on borderline just sugar toffees.

When you come to a place , the stature of a Sofitel From the ACCOR elite stable, you expect basic standards and taste but unfortunately that’s missing.

The fact that it’s in BKC and most people have very little options for a 5 Star experience, plus because of its location the occupancy is high, is the best answer to why it’s half full during these buffets otherwise as per the taste of the food it should be  probably amongst the slowest moving places ever.

Sofitel I have over 11 million people reading this, so I’m saying this with humility please pull up and improve , make prices more competitive and the food seem like it’s made with care for the guests and hopefully the most charm would be back.

Till then all the best!!

name: Love in Langos
description:
Langos is a typical Hungarian food. Nowadays it is a deep fried flatbread, but in the past it was made of the last bits of the bread-dough and baked at the front of a brick or clay oven, to be served hot as the breakfast of the bread-baking day.
Up to the mid 20th century, bread was baked once a week due to the cost of heating up the large oven and the lengthy proces. Because the bread loaf, typical to Hungary, was 6 to 10 pounds each, traditionally they used to bake smaller (1-2 pounds) "cipó" rolls for the evening and the next day. The name lángos (literally meaning "flamed") comes from baking these flat breads.

Love in Lagos - Cafe serves both baked and Fried versions. Lets try some.

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hitchki s one of the most popular restaurants in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), known for its Bollywood-inspired interiors and innovative Indian menu. The moment you walk in, the lively ambience, desi décor, and upbeat music set the tone for a great dining experience. It’s a perfect spot for casual dinners, celebrations, and influencer-friendly content.

We tried a mix of starters, mains, and desserts, and every dish delivered on flavour. The Nacho Nacho Regular was crunchy and addictive, while the Mangalorean Roast Chicken brought authentic coastal flavours to the table. The Godfather Chicken was rich and indulgent, and the Malvani Kolambi Masala stood out with its bold spices and perfectly cooked prawns—easily one of the best seafood dishes in BKC.

Dessert lovers should not miss the Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu, which was smooth, creamy, and beautifully balanced. Paired with their signature drinks like BBC, Hitchki (BKC) proves why it’s among the best restaurants and bars in BKC. Highly recommended for great food, lively vibes, and a memorable dining experience.

featured_reviews.name: Avish Navsaria
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hitchki is a great place to enjoy great vibes with energetic music, Dj and delicious food. They have a great ambience with plenty of safe and amazing seating arrangement. They have great menu with innovative names for all their dishes making it even more exciting to order. The service is very fast and good. The drinks are worth trying and of great innovation. The dishes I tried here were:

1) BIHARI KEBAB: It had Specialty Of Chef Dipesh + Age Old Recipe + Dry Masala Rub +
Tandoori Chicken + Tamatar Chutney. Must try.

2) CAESAR CHICKEN TIKKA: It had Parmesan Malai Marinade + Tandoor Cooked Chicken +
Garlic Parmesan Aioli.

3) ASIAN KITCHEN (CHICKEN): We customised it with Hakka Noodles + Manchurian Garvy + Chicken added. Really tasty and amazing.

4) DESI GIRL COCKTAIL: It has Tequila, Orange Marmalade, Desi Magoi Masala Punch, Red Wine Float + Chakna on top, perfect for a drink.

5) DEEWAR COCKTAIL: It has Whisky + Spiced Jaggery + Bitters + Apple Wood Smoke, amazing presentation and worth trying.

6) GODFATHER CHICKEN: It had Italian Herb Grilled Chicken + Potato Wedges + Sautéed Veg +
Mushroom Pepper Brown Sauce. Perfect for a person who wants to stay on proper diet.

7) Jungle Jungle Pata Chala Hai: A delicious dessert which has Black Forest Pastry 2.0 + Dark Chocolate Mousse + Cherry Mousse +
White Chocolate Ganache + Cherry Gel + Milk Chocolate Shavings.

It’s an all together complete place to visit with great music, food, drinks and service.

featured_reviews.name: Rimita D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Hitchki at BKC, around 7-10 minutes from Kurla station by auto/4 wheeler. It's a vibrant Bollywood themed restaurant and a perfect evening party spot. The presentation of every dish was top-notch.
We tried Masala Soda, Main Toh Superman, Tiger Jhinga Hai, Prawns Jaaye Par, Pressure Cooker Chicken Tikka Biryani, Godfather Chicken, and Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu all impressive, especially the above appetizers which are highly recommended. Chicken lovers must try the Godfather Chicken for its great portion size and taste.
Lotus Biscoff Tiramisu wasn’t overly sweet and made a perfect ending. Loved the playlist too, you will surely vibe on it. Special thanks to Salman and the entire team for the excellent service.

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hitchki BKC is a great spot for a fun lunch or evening out! The vibe is absolutely lovely — beautiful interiors with a cool bar-like feel that makes the whole experience enjoyable.

We tried quite a spread — nachos with cheese, garlic cheese bread, truffle fries, butter chicken seekh kebab, and paneer chilly, and everything was delicious! The truffle fries and seekh kebab were personal favourites. The only miss for us were the butter garlic prawns, which didn't quite live up to the rest of the menu.

Service was prompt and attentive, and we didn't have to wait long for a table at lunch — always a bonus! Valet parking is available which is super convenient for BKC.

Overall a solid dining experience and would definitely recommend it for the vibe and food. Will be back to explore more of the menu! 🙌

Ordered their new Dhurandar chicken which was quite average, the rotis served with it were a disaster, they felt raw hardly even roasted in the tandoor. When we conveyed the same to the person who served us (who also turns out to be the manager) was straight up arrogant and replied that he could only microwave it. Yes sure only forgetting that this isn't some random canteen where he is doing us a favour of serving food.
The basics of service is to first listen here it's the opposite when he gives us such great suggestions.
Such arrogance when the restaurant was almost empty on a weekend lunch would leave the restaurant much emptier in the future as it should be.

If you're looking for tasty South Indian food in a clean and fully vegetarian setting, Balaji Restaurant is a great pick. I tried the masala dosa, sada dosa, and veg cheese sandwich – and everything hit the spot. The masala dosa was crisp and flavorful, with a well-spiced potato filling. The sada dosa really stood out – it was huge and super filling, perfect if you’re really hungry. The veg cheese sandwich was a nice surprise too – cheesy, fresh, and toasted just right.

The place is clean, service is quick, and the overall vibe is comfortable and family-friendly. One of the best parts is that their entire menu is vegetarian, so it’s a worry-free spot for those who prefer or follow a veg diet.

If you’re around Bandra Hill Road or Bandstand and want to try South Indian food, this is hands down one of the best places to go. Highly recommend it for a satisfying and affordable meal!

Dear [Balaji / Manager],

I just wanted to extend my heartfelt thanks for the truly unforgettable meal I received today. Ordering machurian soup and masala dosa sounded like a great idea — until I took my first bite and realized I'd been gifted with a special experience I can only describe as "gastronomic betrayal."

The dosa? A masterpiece of blandness. I’m convinced it was carefully crafted to have absolutely no flavor — a true test of how tasteless food can legally be. Impressive!

But the real star of the show? The chutney. Rotten, sour, and daringly spoiled — it felt like a science experiment gone wrong. Bravo for the courage to serve something that could probably walk off the plate on its own.

Thanks again for redefining my understanding of "meal regret." I’ll be sure to recommend your place to everyone I secretly dislike.

Warm regards,
A very “satisfied” customer

featured_reviews.review_text:
They have Jain food available, which is a plus, but the service and overall experience leave much to be desired. The space is very small, with only 2-3 tables to serve, making it feel cramped. If you ask for water, you’ll get only one glass as they don’t have a jug facility, and if you need a second glass, you’ll have to wait. The food is great, though slightly overpriced. They provide a finger bowl with cold water, but if you ask for warm water, they simply deny it. I requested extra mouth freshener at the end, and the staff looked at us as if we had committed a crime, sternly stating that they only provide two mouth fresheners. The restaurant comes across as stingy in every aspect, whether it’s water or something as small as a mouth freshener. While the Jain food is good, the service and ambiance definitely need improvement.

Edit and reply :

I must say it left a lasting impression on me regarding their service ethics. While the customer shared their experience about limited service and feeling unwelcome when requesting simple extras like a mouth freshener or warm water, the response from the restaurant seemed to justify these shortcomings rather than addressing them empathetically.

Highlighting that the guest asked for extra gravy or carried their own water bottle seems unnecessary and detracts from the core concern of providing a welcoming experience. Great hospitality is about going the extra mile, especially for small gestures that enhance customer satisfaction. Defending such practices as part of policy might reflect on the work ethic and priorities of the establishment.

Good food is important, but customer care and a positive dining experience matter just as much, if not more. I hope the restaurant considers this feedback seriously and strives for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: Kaustubh Havanur
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best places for pure vegetarian food. This place is easily accessible as it is located right on the main road near Sena Bhavan. You can get down at Dadar Metro Station, and as soon as you come onto the main road, the restaurant is right beside it.

Whenever you visit, you will almost always find a rush here. The waiting time can range from 30 minutes to even 1 hour. However, they have now expanded their seating capacity, and there is also a lift available to reach the first floor.

The place is also very reasonably priced. We were a group of four friends and ordered around 7–8 items, yet the total bill was only around ₹1200.

You will find a wide variety of Maharashtrian dishes here, and they have also started serving some South Indian snacks.

Must try: Modak, Aamras, and Misal Pav
You can also try the Batata Vada.

Overall, it is a great place for pure vegetarian food and definitely worth visiting with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Vignesh
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best places for authentic Maharashtrian cuisine with exceptional flavors. We tried the thali, thalipeeth, vada pav, and kurma puri, and every dish was perfectly prepared—well-balanced, flavorful, and needing nothing extra. It’s easy to see why this place is already so popular in Dadar. The only drawback is the compact seating arrangement. Also, be prepared for a waiting time of around 15–30 minutes during peak hours or on busy days.

featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Aaswad Uphar Gruh & Mithai recently and had a proper Maharashtrian भोजन experience.
We tried a variety of items including Puri Bhaji, Seasonal Thali, Puran Poli, Lime Juice, Buttermilk, Kothimbir Vadi, and other traditional dishes. The food overall had that authentic, homely Maharashtrian taste which Aaswad is known for.
👉 Taste:
Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.
👉 Quantity & Quality:
Portion sizes are decent, and ingredients taste fresh. It gives a proper “ghar jaisa khaana” vibe.
👉 Service & Waiting Time:
Had to wait around 40 minutes, which is quite long. The place gets very crowded, especially during peak hours.
👉 Ambience:
Simple, traditional setup. Nothing fancy, but clean and functional. Seating can feel a bit cramped during rush hours.

featured_reviews.name: Rushikesh Kale
featured_reviews.review_text: The best place to try authentic Maharashtrian food! The Misal Pav was amazing, and the Kothimbir Vadi was delicious. We also tried the Pola Usal, which was a real highlight. You must end your meal with the Piyush -it's so refreshing! Highly recommended, but be prepared to wait at least 30 minutes in the queue. It's worth it.

featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad Uphar & Mithai Gruh at Shivaji Park is honestly one of the best places for Maharashtrian food. Their thalipith, misal pav and kothimbir vadi are always delicious and priced very reasonably. The food tastes authentic, the place is clean and hygienic, and you really get that homely Maharashtrian flavour. featured_reviews.name: sk 1
featured_reviews.review_text: Aaswad !! Heaven for Maharashtrian cusine lovers. Great experience and great food. Awesome Misal, Sabudana wada, Batata wada, Thalipeeth and more...to get a seat, we opted for a weekday and early dinner 😃

featured_reviews.name: Sarika Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prepared for a long wait, we were pleasantly surprised to find a table for two upon arrival. Being a week day may have also impacted numbers & wait times which otherwise apparently is a lot.
After a thorough scrutiny of the menu, we ordered pithla bhakri and a chaitra thali.
Pithla bhakri plate comes with two types of bhakris, rice & jowari.
The chaitra thali actually is good for two people which we realised when it arrived. Special mention of the jackfruit bhaaji, kajuchi usal and fresh unadulterated aamras with its natural sweetness & taste. The panah was too thick & sweet for my taste. Missed taking a pic of the thali.
My friend ordered puranpoli ice-cream for dessert & relished it. Again that is a huge portion with three scoops, too much for one person. See the pic :)
Definitely worth a visit to savour Maharashtrian cuisine in an iconic old eatery.
P.S. Five minutes walk from Dadar Aqualine metro station.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

name: Bayroute Maker Maxity, BKC
description: Bayroute is a premium restaurant chain in Mumbai, celebrated for its authentic Middle Eastern and Mediterranean food. It offers a rich selections like hummus & pita, falafel, shawarma, and the indulgent kunafa, along with beautifully curated mezze platters. The immersive ambiance features Moroccan prints, Turkish art, and Arabian-inspired flooring, creating a vibrant yet elegant setting that transports diners straight to the Mediterranean. featured_reviews.name: Arjika S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute BKC never disappoints — but this time, they’ve truly outdone themselves with their Kebab & Meze Festival. The moment you step in, the ambience wraps you in warm golden lights and Mediterranean charm — it’s luxe yet cozy, elegant yet soulful.

I started my meal with the Ruyhan, a bright orange cooler that’s refreshing and slightly citrusy — the perfect start to a rich Middle Eastern feast. Their Zaffrani Chai was another star — aromatic, creamy, and comforting, with just the right hint of saffron.

Coming to the food — the Moroccan Chermoula Prawns were perfectly grilled and bursting with smoky, tangy flavours, while the Djej Al Jibneh was every cheese lover’s dream come true — tender chicken layered with molten cheese that melts in your mouth.

For mains, I tried the Kebab Koobideh, and it was absolute perfection — juicy, buttery kebabs served with saffron rice that complemented every bite. The textures, the balance of spice, and that authentic Persian touch made it unforgettable.

And of course, no visit to Bayroute is complete without dessert — the Chocolate Kunafa was the ultimate showstopper! Crisp golden strands on top, gooey chocolate inside, and just the right level of sweetness — the perfect ending to a luxurious meal.

Overall, Bayroute continues to deliver an experience that goes beyond just food — it’s a full-on sensory journey through the Middle East. Every dish feels thoughtfully crafted, the staff is super courteous, and the attention to detail is immaculate.

✨ Must Try:
•	Moroccan Chermoula Prawns 🦐
•	Djej Al Jibneh 🧀
•	Kebab Koobideh 🥩
•	Chocolate Kunafa 🍫
•	Zaffrani Chai ☕

Whether you’re a Middle Eastern food lover or someone just exploring new flavours — this festival is not to be missed!

featured_reviews.name: Radhika Gokani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bayroute in BKC is one of those places that instantly sets the mood the moment you walk in. The ambience is warm, elegant, and inviting, with beautiful Middle Eastern accents that make it perfect for a relaxed meal or a special outing. It feels upscale yet comfortable, and the overall vibe adds so much to the dining experience.

We started with the Hummus Bayroute, which was incredibly smooth, rich, and full of flavor — easily one of the best hummus options on the table, paired perfectly with fresh bread. The cottage cheese shawarma was a pleasant surprise, well-spiced, hearty, and packed with textures that made every bite satisfying. The koshari was comforting and wholesome, with a great balance of lentils, rice, and sauce, making it both filling and flavorful.

For desserts, the baklava was crisp, nutty, and just the right amount of sweet, ending the meal on a high note. The Arabic date palm shake was indulgent, naturally sweet, and refreshing, while the Thai Meets Middle East drink was a fun, creative fusion — refreshing, unique, and definitely worth trying.

Overall, Bayroute BKC delivers on ambience, quality, and flavors, making it a great spot for Middle Eastern food lovers and anyone looking for a refined yet cozy dining experience. Definitely a place you’d want to revisit.

featured_reviews.name: shubham sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Bayroute recently and honestly, it was such a lovely experience. The place has this calm, aesthetic vibe with warm lighting and cozy seating that instantly makes you feel comfortable. The ambience is beautiful and unique; every corner looks picture-perfect. The presentation of each dish was stunning. Every plate looked thoughtfully crafted with attention to detail.
The food was rich in flavor and beautifully balanced. The Greek Goddess and Muhammara had fresh, authentic Mediterranean flavors, while the Lavash Crust Chicken Kabsa was perfectly cooked and full of aroma. My favorite was definitely the Salted Caramel Baklava Shaikh thick, creamy, nutty, and just the right amount of sweet. It felt like the perfect dessert to end the meal.
The Moroccan Charmoula and Dijaj Tria had a lovely mix of spices, giving that true Middle Eastern taste. Everything tasted fresh and flavorful without being too heavy.

Also, a big thumbs-up to their hospitality. The staff was warm, polite, and very attentive, making the whole experience even better. Overall, Bayroute is that perfect blend of great food, beautiful ambience, and amazing service. Totally worth a visit!

featured_reviews.name: Veeni Saumil Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a lovely experience at Bayroute, BKC.
Bkc Restaurants have some special charm.  The place has a very warm and beautiful ambience with soft lighting and Arabic-inspired decor. The hot-air-balloon style ceiling and overall setup really add to the charm and make it feel special.
We started with our drinks which were refreshing and set the tone for a good evening.
Coming to the food, we enjoyed everything we tried.
The Pide Pizza was soft, flavourful and really comforting.
The Fatar Baklava with mushroom filling was one of the best dishes of the night, rich and literally melt-in-the-mouth.
The Cottage Cheese Shawarma was my personal favourite, something I would happily go back for.
We also tried the Koshari, their popular Arabic rice dish, which tasted wholesome and nicely balanced.
We ended the meal with their Baklava dessert, which came with a fun presentation and tasted amazing.
Overall, Bayroute BKC is a great place if you love Middle Eastern food or just want a nice dining experience with good ambience, flavourful food and a relaxed, premium feel.

featured_reviews.name: J G Irani
featured_reviews.review_text:
All routes are leading to BAYROUTE at BKC, Mumbai. No doubt, it's the most popular restaurant for specialties which include Middle Eastern, Arabic and Mediterranean dishes. The cuisine delivers delicacies like melt in your mouth kebabs, authentic hummus, signature baklava, pides, pizzas etc in veg and non veg preparations. Must try their Sumac De Light,
Smoky Rum N Raisins cocktails and in starters Kebab Joojeh,
Kebab Halabi was the highlight. The main course of
Machboos Al Kuzu and
Lavash Crust Chicken Kabsa was a delicious wholesome delight. At the top was the dessert Baklava. BAYROUTE, BKC restaurant is also known for its sophisticated ambiance which offers a unique fine dining experience.
